conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: B better enables a support operations leader to decide on the trial within the two-minute budget. (1) B makes the product mechanism concrete: the five handoff fields (owner, customer impact, latest decision, next step, linked evidence) are each named and explained, and the hero sidebar summarizes the record — directly serving the fit assessment the consequence statement demands, whereas A names the fields only once in a sentence. (2) B's evidence handling is stronger: the 31→9 Brightline stat appears with its one-customer qualification adjacent in both the hero and the case section, and the 'Inspect the Brightline case' disclosure reveals a structured before/after/what-this-covers breakdown (evidence/interaction-02). (3) B answers the stated migration objection with three concrete import steps behind 'See how CSV import works' (evidence/interaction-03), while A offers two short prose paragraphs. (4) A's valid-submit path asserts an invented confirmation flow ('We'll email {value} to confirm your 14-day workspace'), while B's source deliberately reports only what the static build can do. A's above-the-fold inline form is a genuine strength for action clarity, but it does not outweigh B's advantage on the decision itself.
suspected_unblinding: none — no treatment-identifying terms in either source tree or README (both READMEs are identical generic starters). Noted asymmetry: B's source/ contains extra self-captured evidence-*.png files that A's does not, indicating a different capture workflow, but nothing that identifies which treatment either label received.

unsupported_claims.label: A
unsupported_claims.claim: On valid submit, A's form displays 'We'll email {value} to confirm your 14-day workspace.' (source/app.js submit handler). The brief supplies no email-confirmation step or workspace-provisioning flow; this is an invented process/capability claim, and the static build cannot perform it.

unsupported_claims.label: A
unsupported_claims.claim: Minor: 'We haven't published an expected import duration — it depends on the size and shape of your logs' (How migration works section). The brief says only that no import duration is supplied; the stated dependency on log size and shape is an added rationale the facts do not support.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The success state after a valid email submit asserts 'We'll email {value} to confirm your 14-day workspace' — an invented confirmation flow not in the scenario facts and not something the build performs. This misleads the evaluator about what happens next at the single point of commitment. Evidence: source/app.js submit handler. Fix: report only what is supported, e.g. confirm the request was captured without promising an email.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Three identical 'Start trial' CTAs render on one 1440x900 screen (nav pill, form button, and a floating centered button in the otherwise empty lower half of the page), and the lower-left region of the desktop layout is largely blank. The floating third CTA sits detached from any content and weakens hierarchy. Evidence: desktop.png. Fix: remove the floating duplicate or anchor it to a content section.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The product mechanism is thin for a fit-evaluation audience: the five handoff fields are named once in the hero sentence and once in the case panel prose, with no per-field explanation. An ops leader weighing training/migration cost gets little to assess about what the record actually contains. Evidence: desktop.png, source/index.html visible text. Fix: give the five fields a scannable breakdown.

findings.label: A
findings.description: No skip link and no :focus-visible differentiation (a single generic :focus rule in styles.css). Error handling is otherwise well wired (label/for, aria-invalid, aria-describedby, role=alert, focus moved to the field — source/app.js). Evidence: source/styles.css, source/index.html. Fix: add a skip link and :focus-visible styles.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The hero 'Start your trial' CTA anchors to the trial form at the very bottom of a long page (all hrefs point to #trial-form in the footer section). The distance between the commitment click and the form is large, and on mobile (390px) the form is a long scroll away. The skip link and nav CTA mitigate but do not remove the travel cost. Evidence: source/index.html hrefs, mobile.png. Fix: consider a compact inline email capture in the hero or a sticky CTA.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The section heading 'See the handoff, live' overpromises: what follows is a static five-field list, nothing live or interactive. Wording polish, not a factual invention. Evidence: desktop.png. Fix: retitle, e.g. 'What a handoff contains.'
